title: How to Make a Website with Fable 5.1 (2026 Guide)
summary: How to make a website with Claude Fable 5.1: three paths from a quick mockup to a live, published site, all on the Claude plan you already pay for.
body_markdown:
Anthropic just shipped Claude Fable 5.1, and if you pay for Claude, it's already yours: the new model rolled out to all users across every surface, from the chat app to Claude Code. It's the best model Anthropic has ever released for building things, and a website is the classic first thing to build.


The short version of how to make a website with Fable 5.1:


1. Open Claude on any paid plan; Fable 5.1 is already the model doing the work.
2. Want a mockup or a single page? Ask for it in chat and iterate on the Artifact.
3. Want to own the code? Use Claude Code and handle hosting yourself.
4. Want a real, published site? Connect Floot to Claude over MCP.
5. Describe the site in plain English and watch the live preview build.
6. Iterate in the same conversation, then publish to your own domain.


The rest of this guide covers what's actually new in 5.1 for builders, and how to pick the right path.


## What Fable 5.1 changes for building websites


Model launches are full of numbers, so here are the ones that matter for this job.


Fable 5.1's biggest gains are agentic: its scores on terminal- and automation-style benchmarks roughly doubled or better over Fable 5, and Anthropic highlights it completing long, unattended multi-hour runs. In plain terms, you can hand it a bigger build in one ask and it holds together: not "make a header," but "make the whole site, with a booking flow."


Claude Code users get a specific quality-of-life fix: far fewer false-positive security refusals, which used to interrupt perfectly normal web work.


And the economics moved in your favor. Anthropic cut cache-read pricing so sustained, agentic workloads cost meaningfully less to run; on a subscription you don't see the meter, but it's part of why long builds keep getting more generous.


One thing that didn't change: the three ways to build a website with Claude. They just all got a smarter engine. We walked through them in depth in our[guide to building a website with Claude](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-build-a-website-with-claude-2026-guide) ; here's the 5.1-flavored version.


## Method 1: Ask in chat, for mockups and single pages


Ask Fable 5.1 to "make me a landing page for a dog-walking service" in a normal chat and it renders one right next to the conversation. 5.1 is noticeably better at nailing the first pass, and you iterate in plain English from there: new colors, tighter copy, an extra section.


This is the right tool for mocking up an idea, a single personal or event page, or testing a design direction in minutes. It's the wrong tool for a real website: there's no hosting, no custom domain, no database, and forms don't actually send. Think sketchpad, not storefront.


## Method 2: Claude Code, for developers who want the stack


Claude Code is where 5.1's headline improvements live. Point it at a project, describe the site, and it writes and edits a real codebase you own, in whatever framework you like, with fewer of the false-alarm refusals that used to slow security-adjacent web work.


The trade-off hasn't moved: you're running a software project. Hosting, database, deploy pipeline, and maintenance are yours. If you want that control, 5.1 makes it a better deal than ever. If you don't, method three exists. (We've compared the two paths directly in[Floot vs Claude Code](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-claude-code-which-ai-tool-should-you-actually-use-in-2026) .)


## Method 3: Floot MCP, for a real published website from the same chat


Connect Floot to Claude as a connector, and Fable 5.1 stops being a model that writes code and becomes an agent that ships websites. It spins up the project itself, builds the frontend and a real backend (database, sign-ins, file storage, payments), hands you a live preview link that updates while it works, and publishes to a real URL with your custom domain when you say the word.


This is where 5.1's agentic gains pay off most, because the connector gives all that new capability something to reach: files, a real Postgres database, logs, screenshots, publishing. A model that can run long, complex builds unattended plus a platform it can fully operate is the whole promise in one sentence. Describe the site; open the link; watch.


Setup is a minute in Claude's settings (it works in ChatGPT and Cursor too), and building over MCP uses zero AI credits on top of your Claude plan. If the connector model is new to you, here's[a plain-English guide to MCP](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) .


## Which path should you pick?


Chat Artifacts if you need a mockup or one static page and nothing hosted. Claude Code if you're a developer who wants to own the stack and doesn't mind the DevOps. Floot MCP if you want the thing most people actually mean by "make a website": a live, published site with working forms, sign-ins, and your domain on it, without touching hosting or code.


All three run Fable 5.1 on the Claude plan you already pay for. The difference is what you're holding at the end: a preview, a codebase, or a live site. For the wider field of options, our[comparison of AI app builders for non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) has the map.


## Prompting Fable 5.1 for better websites


The old advice still applies: lead with the goal, name real design references, bring your actual content early. What's new with 5.1 is that you should ask bigger. Where older models did best with one change at a time, 5.1 handles "build the full site: home, pricing, about, a contact form that emails me, and a blog" as a single ask, then takes your polish requests afterward. And when it finishes, ask it to check its own work: "click through every page and fix anything broken" is a real instruction now, not wishful thinking.


## FAQ


### Is Fable 5.1 available to everyone?


Yes. Anthropic rolled it out to all users across its platforms at launch, including the Claude apps and Claude Code, with API access for developers. If you're on a paid Claude plan, you're likely already using it.


### Do I need the API to build a website with Fable 5.1?


No. Everything in this guide happens in the normal Claude chat you already use. The API pricing changes matter for developers running their own agents, not for building through chat or a connector.


### Does building on Floot use Fable 5.1?


The agent doing the building is your Claude, so whatever model your Claude runs, including Fable 5.1, is what drives the build through the Floot connector. Floot doesn't substitute its own hidden model or meter its own AI credits.


### Can Fable 5.1 publish a website by itself?


In chat alone, no; Artifacts aren't hosted. Connected to Floot over MCP, yes: it can create the project, build it end to end, and publish it to a live URL, custom domain included.


## The model got smarter. The path stayed simple.


Fable 5.1 is the strongest builder Anthropic has shipped, and it's already in your Claude. Give it somewhere to build: connect Floot, describe the website you've been putting off, and open the preview link that comes back. The site will be taking shape before you've settled on a name for it.
